description: The EXTREMES OF THE DECLARED SPANS, reached over a complete successful pass of app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl. Every other case of this program seeds values from the middle of each span's range, and a value from the middle cannot show whether a span is being carried at its declared width or merely at the width the value happens to need. This case drives each numeric span to its lowest representable value, to its midpoint and to its highest, in three records read in one pass, so that DISPLAY's defining property is asserted: it concatenates its operands at their DECLARED widths, never at their significant widths, so no value here may be shortened, re-padded, re-aligned, trimmed of a leading zero or trimmed of a trailing space. Deriving the three records, span by span from app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy rather than from prose. ACCT-ID is PIC 9(11), an unsigned eleven-digit span, so its bounds are 00000000000 and 99999999999 written out to all eleven positions. The five monetary spans - ACCT-CURR-BAL, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT - are each PIC S9(10)V99, which is twelve digit positions and therefore twelve stored characters: ten before the implied decimal point and two after it, the point itself occupying no byte. Not one of the 28 copybooks in app/cpy declares COMP-3 or PACKED-DECIMAL, so every persisted numeric span in this system is zoned DISPLAY and the sign travels as an overpunch in the trailing byte. The positive overpunch series is '{' for digit 0 and 'A' through 'I' for digits 1 through 9, so the three images follow mechanically: 00000000000{ is eleven zeros closed by '{', which is a twelfth digit of 0 with a positive sign, and represents 0.00 - the smallest value a positive span of this PICTURE carries; 55555555555E is closed by 'E', a twelfth digit of 5, and represents 555555555.55 - the midpoint, present so that a translation which happened to be correct only at the two ends is still caught; and 99999999999I is closed by 'I', a twelfth digit of 9, and represents 9999999999.99 - the largest value the span carries, every one of its twelve digit positions occupied. The overpunch byte is data and not decoration: it must survive deserialisation, seeding, decoding and rendering untouched, which is exactly what pinning the raw image asserts. The non-numeric spans are NOT invented. Each is taken verbatim from row 0 of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt at its own offset, so every record here is production-shaped and only the numerics are driven to their bounds: ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS at offset 11 is 'Y', ACCT-OPEN-DATE at 48 is 2014-11-20, ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE at 58 is 2025-05-20, ACCT-REISSUE-DATE at 68 is 2025-05-20, ACCT-ADDR-ZIP at 102 is A000000000 and ACCT-GROUP-ID at 112 is ten spaces. The copybook's misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE is preserved exactly as it is spelt rather than corrected to ACCT-EXPIRATION-DATE, because the field name is part of the contract that field-for-field diffing binds to and renaming it would silently break the comparison rather than fail it. ACCT-GROUP-ID's ten spaces are significant and are the reason its labelled line is 35 characters and not 25: a translation that trimmed a wholly blank alphanumeric span would shorten that line and be reported here. Deriving the record width, mechanically. The twelve named spans measure 11 + 1 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 = 122 bytes and sit at offsets 0, 11, 12, 24, 36, 48, 58, 68, 78, 90, 102 and 112; FILLER PIC X(178) begins at offset 122 and closes the record at 122 + 178 = 300, which is the RECLN the copybook's own header states. FILLER is emitted as 178 spaces and is never omitted: drop it and the record is 122 bytes, every offset past it is wrong, and ParityHarness refuses the row outright because a fixed-width dataset cannot hold a ragged row. The three ACCT-ID values are also chosen so that no row here can be mistaken for stored fixture data - acctdata.txt carries 00000000001 through 00000000050, and 00000000000, 55555555555 and 99999999999 are none of them. The expected SYSOUT is 41 lines, which is 1 + (3 x 13) + 1, and the 13 is not a choice: each record is displayed TWICE by two different paragraphs. 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD, performed from inside the '00' arm of the read paragraph at L96, emits eleven labelled field lines at L119-L129 and a separator of 49 hyphens at L130; then the mainline's own DISPLAY ACCOUNT-RECORD at L78 emits the raw 300-byte image. Each label is its copybook field name padded to 25 characters including the terminating colon, so every line width is a sum and not an assertion of taste: ACCT-ID 25 + 11 = 36, ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS 25 + 1 = 26, each of the five monetary lines 25 + 12 = 37, each of the three date lines 25 + 10 = 35, ACCT-GROUP-ID 25 + 10 = 35, the separator 49, and the raw image 300. The banners are the literals at L71 and L85 transcribed verbatim, at 38 and 36 characters, and they are byte-identical to the first and last lines case03 expects on an empty dataset. Note which span is ABSENT from the labelled lines: ACCT-ADDR-ZIP is declared by the copybook and stored in every record, yet the paragraph labels only eleven of the twelve named spans and never labels that one - so here it is observable only inside the 300-byte raw image. case09 pins that omission directly. Read order is key order, not insertion order: app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl:L29-L33 declares ACCTFILE as ORGANIZATION INDEXED, ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY FD-ACCT-ID. The three records are seeded in ASCENDING key order here, so browse order and seeding order coincide deliberately: this case varies width and nothing else, and case20 is the one that varies insertion order against a fixed set of widths. Keeping the two variables in separate cases is what makes a failure in either attributable. Termination, statement by statement. The loop at L74-L81 runs four iterations: three reads report '00' at L94, each moving 0 into APPL-RESULT so the 88 APPL-AOK condition at L62 holds and each record is displayed twice as above; the fourth read reports '10' at L98, moving 16 into APPL-RESULT so APPL-AOK is false while the 88 APPL-EOF condition at L63 holds, and L108 moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE. That arm carries no DISPLAY, and the inner IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' at L77 is then false, so the fourth iteration adds no line at all - end of file is silent and emits neither a diagnostic nor a records-processed summary, which is the property case03 isolates on an empty dataset and which holds identically here after three records. 9000-ACCTFILE-CLOSE then sees '00' at L154 and L155's SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT leaves 0, so APPL-AOK holds and L160 CONTINUEs without a message; L85 displays the closing banner and L87 GOBACKs. The return code is 0 because the program never touches RETURN-CODE on a path that completes, so no error literal, no rendered file status and no ABENDING PROGRAM line appears anywhere in these 41 lines. That close paragraph's arithmetic idiom - ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT at L152, SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT at L155 and ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT at L157 - is peculiar to it, where the open and read paragraphs use a plain MOVE 8, MOVE 0 and MOVE 12 for the same three values; it is preserved as written rather than normalised, and on this successful path only the first two of the three run and both leave APPL-RESULT at 0. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT PIN, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. It does not reach the fatal ELSE arm of 9000-ACCTFILE-CLOSE at L156-L166, whose literal is 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' at L162 and whose return code would be 12 from the ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT at L157, and it does not pretend to. That arm is not reachable from ANY BATCH_JOB parity case of this program, for reasons that are properties of the contract rather than of this case: the arm needs the dataset to stop being addressable BETWEEN the browse and the close, which is a temporal condition no seeded dataset expresses; ParityCase refuses a BATCH_JOB case a screenRequest, and with it the forced repository outcomes an online case may declare; the RepositoryOperation set a forced outcome may name is read, readForUpdate, readNext, startBrowse, write, rewrite and delete, and contains no open and no close at all; and app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L22 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT01C with no PARM, so inventing a job parameter to carry an instruction would misstate that JCL contract. The arm is not left unasserted - it is driven where it can be driven, by AccountBalanceJobTest, which scripts a failing CLOSE over a complete pass and requires the opening banner, the record's thirteen lines, the L162 literal, the rendered status and the 'ABENDING PROGRAM' line at L170, requires that the L85 banner is absent, and requires return code 12. Equally out of reach here is the numeric ELSE arm of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at L184-L187, which would render a two-digit status such as '38' as 0, 0, 3, 8 by moving '0000' into IO-STATUS-04 and then the status into IO-STATUS-04(3:2), giving FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0038 after the 20-character literal whose NNNN is part of the literal itself and not a placeholder: the only fatal status this translation's backend reports begins with '9', so every fatal arm reachable from a case of this program takes the extended arm at L177-L183 instead, and CBACT01CParityTest requires every case whose return code is non-zero to end with the image composed from AccountRepository.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS followed by the abend line and to carry one of only two error literals as its third-from-last line. Recording both limits here, rather than encoding an expectation the harness cannot produce, is what keeps this gate honest: an unreachable expectation does not strengthen a suite, it breaks it. Nothing is written. CBACT01C opens ACCTFILE for INPUT and issues no WRITE and no REWRITE - the mandated class name AccountBalanceJob notwithstanding, the program computes no balance - so 'expectedWrites' being empty asserts that positively rather than expressing a lack of interest. All three records are pinned byte for byte on the final-state channel, read back from the dataset rather than echoed from the seed, which is what makes 'the three stored records are still exactly the three stored records, at their extreme values' a real assertion about a class with that name; and the dataset-level expectation of exactly 3 rows at 300 bytes states what no row expectation can, namely that no FOURTH row appeared and that the dataset is still 300 bytes wide. The case is deterministic: what it declares is a fixed literal set of three record images, and it carries no wall-clock value and no random value. It declares no job parameter, because app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L22 is a bare EXEC PGM= with no PARM. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key, ACCTFILE, which is the DD name at app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L25; no fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears here, because those live only in application.yml. Every byte of every seeded row and every character of every expected line is US-ASCII, the code page of app/data/ASCII and of ParityHarness.FIXTURE_CHARSET, named explicitly and never left to the platform default. Provenance: statically derived by reading app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl paragraph by paragraph, cross-checked against the byte layout of app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, the DD and PARM contract of app/jcl/READACCT.jcl and the real fixture data in app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, and against the constants published by AccountBalanceJob, AccountRepository, AbendException and FileStatus. Nothing here was captured from, recorded against or replayed from a run of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment - there is no z/OS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE service exists to link the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L173 - and that substitution of the provenance of the expected values, and nothing else about the gate, is the escalated deviation recorded as risk R-A.
